response.consequence: A user who turns on the sqlExpressions feature flag still cannot create SQL expressions, because every SQL query is rejected at parse time. The `NewSQLCommand` path in ReadQuery is unreachable. If the stub is meant to disable the feature, the dead flag check hides that. If it is meant to honour the flag, the logic is broken.
response.explanation: enableSqlExpressions sets `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)`, so the variable holds the negation of the flag. It then returns false when that negation is true. The fall-through path also returns false. Every path returns false, whatever the flag value. The `QueryTypeSQL` case in ReadQuery therefore always returns "sqlExpressions is not implemented", even when the feature flag is on. The flag check does nothing, and the inverted variable name suggests a logic error.
response.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false and inverts the feature flag
